When in Malacca I wouldn't missed my makan for the world be it lunch or dinner at any of the peranakan restaurants that have been mushrooming all over Malacca particularly in Taman Melaka Raya. I simply take a leisurely stroll from Hatten hotel to my all-time favourite true blue peranakan Amy Heritage Nyonya Cuisine. I can't help but noticed the menu was laminated and new compared the previous one was old and looked antique enough to be sent to Malacca museum for preservation. Again the over-friendly Amy's husband passed the menu and before he could recommend the dishes; I reminded him this wasn't my first time. We ordered our best-loved ayam buah keluak, kerabu bendi (steamed lady's finger top with fresh red chillies shallots and daun limau perut) my personal favourite die die must order. For prawn we tried the sambal tumis udang with petai. We did not call in advance to make reservations which normally is a must if you do not wish to go all the way and be disappointed if the restaurant is fully-booked. We were lucky as we arrived at 6.30pm though there were already walk-in diners but most tables were reserved. Since only the two of us, he was kind enough to accomodate us with a table brought from outside the restaurant set up near the entrance.All the the three dishes served on out tables less than 15minutes. After the last time early last year we had the same food especially ayam buah keluak and the steamed bendi was still superbly good though the sambal udang prawn with petai "not soo pedas". Maybe Amy trying to tone down the spiciness of the sambal tumis. Honestly still the best nyonya food I have had in Malacca and I promised uncle Lim...I'll be back!!!

Pelita Nasi Kandar in SS15, Subang Jaya was one of my favorite go to place whenever I need quick & cheap fix. However, my recent experiences lately had been disappointing. See, the night manager is this middle age man with a cool mustache who happens to be an impeccably competent staff. That's not the case for some of the rest. My first offputting incident started about 5 months ago. I requested for tissue and guess what the waiter did? He pointed at the tissue box near the counter implying that I should take it myself. It was qickly resolved by another staff who saw it, eventually got it for me. Second incident which was 2 months ago, I queued and there it was my turn so I walked to the fried chicken till to tell the chandi man the part I wanted.. which is the last one. I suppose he got sidetracked and went to put rice for another customer while I was walking to that fried parts's till, followed by this next person ultimately getting it. I walked out without saying anything or causing a scene. I kept my patience, grace since they obviously didn't need the money of a multimillionaire in laidback clothings and would prefer some average Joe's who look more like the perfect local. Now, the last incident which hugely infuriated me. Same scenario, only that there was plenty of the specific chicken part. After queing at 3 customers and finally come to my turn, I told the chandi man no rice for me please and I only wanted to tapau the chicken. Again, while I walked to the till they got sidetracked by some next customer who happens to be our stereotypical Malay 'brader'. Without holding back, I insisted him to get my order sorted with "Now"/"Sekarang" as he was bustling on that bloke's vegetables, curry on his plate of rice and enormously snubbed my request. Telling me to 'Wait'. Seriously?Disdained, I called the chandi man an "Idiot"/ "Bodoh" (He knows me as a customer too well) with a loud voice and stormed out the restaurant, scoring them with a final line of "I came first in the queue, you should've just served me first!"/ "Saya datang dulu di beratur, awak patut buat makanan saya dulu!" with them looking indignant, not understanding what they did wrong big time. Both remarks in Bahasa of course. If some of you might have noticed, I wore dark grey V-neck and that was the case there. I guess I wouldn't ever want to come here anymore, and I commitedly mean it. Pelita Nasi Kandar is one of those eateries that reminds you why sometime you being sporting and humble has its price. The staffs apparently so are dodgy in manners and takes advantage of your pleasantry. Anyway, if you're immensely hungry and would like to know a restaurant that you can simply skip queue.. I do highly recommend Pelita SS15.

It was a weekend of makan (eat) and shopping spree in Melaka and Amy Heritage Nonya Cuisine) was on our check list. Having made advance reservation via a phone call. We were not disappointed with our lunch there. The kueh pie were tasty. The assam ikan was sedap too and so was the udang (prawns) masak nanas. The nonya mee was very sedap very similiar to my mum's home cooked version. The chicken cooked with candle nut (buah keras) was yummy. But the otak was a disappointment, as the rempah has a very strong kunyit (turmeric) taste which overwhelm the flavour. The chap chye was disappointing, the gravy was too sweet and the cabbage was hard. We had chendol for dessert and it was ok. The gula melaka was very wangi (fragrant) but quite diluted. Using freshly squeezed coconut (santan) would have enhanced the flavour further. Overall we enjoyed the lunch very much. And will return to try the buah keluak and other nonya dishes. A note of advice. Do call to make reservation at least a day or two in advance.

My family and I (5 of us) visited Rebung on Monday, 1 June for dinner and it was the MOST HORRIBLE Malay buffet dinner we had! 1. The food was cold.2. The Nasi Hijau (Green Rice) was stale (basi). It was slimy and smelt horrible. When we informed the staff, they simply said, "Oh Okay" and took the pot away... NO APOLOGY!3. The buffet items were not labeled and so we do not know what dishes it was.4. The staff also could not advise the names of the gravy as he is a Filipino.5. We had to continuously asked for our glasses to be topped up as the service staff was busy chatting among themselves inside the restaurant.6. The grill (we paid more for dinner bcoz of the grill) was also cold. Cold chicken wings and hard chewy gummy lamb. When asked why they do not keep a small flame under the buffet, the reply was that it would dry up the food.7. The restaurant was empty. Besides us, there were only two other small group of 2-3 diners. However, when we called the day earlier, we were told to make reservations.8. The dessert spread was lean with only malay kueh kueh (cakes) which looks like it had been left on the buffet since lunch.10. Upon payment of $215 at cashier, not a word of "Thank You" from the lady manager. 11. The cutlery are not very clean.12. I had a little bit of diarrhoea when I got back to the hotel.So if you really must go to WASTE your money and experience HORRIBLE Food and ATROCIOUS Service, perhaps you can go during lunch when the food is hot and freshly prepared or when the Chef is in-house (I suppose). Otherwise, do not waste time at this restaurant as the dinner and service sucks big time! For RM43/person, you can enjoy a much better dinner at anywhere else in KL for half the price.In short, Indah Kata dari Rasa! (Words are better than the real stuff)

column9: Back in the 90s and early 2000, Lok Thian is the household name and the go to place for makan. Dim sum, Chinese, Japanese or Thai cuisines...their restaurant used to be the place be. But these days...service wise is really bad. On Christmas morning we decided to have brunch with the in-laws. They arrived first and were seated upstairs but nobody came to take their order, my sister in-law went downstairs to order but was chased back up. When we arrived, we took the liberty to go back down to place our order. After placing our orders we sat and waited. Only some of our orders arrived and the drinks came very late. After waiting for some time and our food didn't seem to be coming we decided to leave and when we went to pay they had the audacity to charge us for the food which weren't served. Only after insisting we didn't get the food did they later waived the amount. We  came to support local businesses and as the world is opening up more people are going out to eat with family and friends yet they don't seem to have enough staff to take orders and serve food.  How to help such local businesses when they don't help themselves to improve and deliver quality service? Really spoil our mood for the day. I'll think twice if I ever have to come here in the future...

I don't understand why people queue for this. I have had way better chicken rice balls outside of Melaka. You can try heading to the Klang Valley and you'll be surprised how bad this one is compared to the ones found over there. I used to frequent Chung Wah and thought it was the best in Melaka but even that has dropped in standards, and is currently closed without notice. Hoe Kee's chicken was bland, the rice was very normal. You can get authentic Hainanese chicken rice (not in ball form though) that is so fragrant and flavorful you can eat it plates of it without the chicken. Try Kedai Nasi Dan Ayam along Petaling Street and then you will know what real Hainan chicken rice tastes like. This will be my last visit to Hoe Kee.

I grew up eating here. My personal childhood favourite was Uncle "Lek Koo"s beef soup noodles - with beef balls, tender beef strips served with real beef broth - he'd have none of the ajinomoto version. New Hollywood used to have a real grumpy popiah basah uncle who would only sell you his popiah if he was in a good mood. But his popiah was so good, folks would put up with his bad moods just to have it. Now Uncle "Lek Koo" and the grumpy popiah man are no longer around - well at least not when i went there last week - but the food is still great. New Hollywood also still serves the famous Ipoh egg caramel custard. The roti telur goyang. The char kway teow is also very nice. I enjoyed the Siamese laksa on that Sunday. Apparently the brother of HRH the late Sultan of Perak lives further down the road from this kedai kopi and some members of the Perak royal family makan here too. And yes, it's all halal. It reminds me of the old days when Malaysians of all races and religions could eat together in a kopitiam.
